title: Pro-etale scalar mate restricts to the specified projection arrow
statement:
Let $a:A\to B$ be a map of finite commutative rings and $u:T\to V$ any scheme map. Use ordinary unbounded constant-ring module derived categories on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Put $S_W=-\otimes^L_{A_W}B_W$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and let $U_W$ be exact scalar restriction [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. The scalar adjunction $S_W\dashv U_W$ is the representative-normalized one of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Let $\lambda_u:u_B^{-1}S_V\xrightarrow{\sim}S_Tu_A^{-1}$ be the canonical tensor inverse-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. For $M\in D(T_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ let $\chi_{u,M}:S_VRu_*^AM\to Ru_*^BS_TM$ be the $u_B^{-1}\dashv Ru_*^B$ adjunct [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of $S_T(\varepsilon^A_{u,M})\circ\lambda_{u,Ru_*^AM}$. Under the canonical identifications $U_WS_WN\cong N\otimes_A^LB_W$ and $U_VRu_*^B\cong Ru_*^AU_T$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction], restriction of $\chi_{u,M}$ is the specified projection morphism $\pi^A_{u;M,B_V}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. In particular its counit equation is
$$\varepsilon^B_{u,S_TM}\circ u_B^{-1}(\chi_{u,M})=S_T(\varepsilon^A_{u,M})\circ\lambda_{u,Ru_*^AM}.$$
All identifications are natural and no boundedness or flatness of $a$ is assumed.

proof.text: Write $L_R=u_R^{-1}$ and $G_R=Ru_*^R$ for $R=A,B$. There are canonical natural identifications $h_{W,N}:U_WS_WN\cong N\otimes^L_{A_W}B_W$. Indeed [lem-pur-change-of-rings-tensor-comparison] identifies restricted ordinary change of rings with the sheaf tensor, naturally in the module. Choose its canonical tensor identification: before sheafification it is the identity on the balanced tensor, with the symmetry putting the coefficient last [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Restriction changes only the action, so the underlying associated abelian sheaf is the same. For a K-flat resolution $P\to N$, [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] computes $S_WN$ by $P\otimes_{A_W}B_W$; the same complex computes $N\otimes^L_{A_W}B_W$ by the one-K-flat-factor computation in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. These identifications are natural in resolutions and hence in $N$. They use the representative normalization of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]: the scalar unit is $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, and scalar extension of a map is tensor of that map with $1$. In particular $h_{W,N'}U_WS_W(f)=(f\otimes1)h_{W,N}$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] with $R_W=A_W$, $S_W=B_W$ and their constant-coefficient inverse-image identifications $c_A:u^{-1}A_V\xrightarrow{\sim}A_T$, $c_B:u^{-1}B_V\xrightarrow{\sim}B_T$, which are isomorphisms of ring sheaves by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. The square $a_Tc_A=c_B\,u^{-1}(a_V)$ commutes: by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] both sides are adjoint to the maps $A_V\to u_*B_T$ sending a constant section $x$ to the constant section $a(x)$, and these sections generate the sheafified constant presheaf. It gives $b:U_TL_B\cong L_AU_V$ and $d:U_VG_B\cong G_AU_T$, with their stated adjunction compatibility. The ordinary unbounded operations here are exactly [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]: inverse image is exact and direct image is computed using K-injectives. Thus this application does not require restriction of scalars to preserve K-injective complexes; $d$ is the canonical composite-ringed-topos comparison of the cited statement.

source.place: Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map; Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), and 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition); explicit coefficient-change specialization

proof.text:
Let $v:L_AB_V=A_T\otimes_{u^{-1}A_V}u^{-1}B_V\cong B_T$ be the constant-coefficient identification induced by $c_A^{-1}$ and $c_B$ [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], and put $\mu^B_N=(1\otimes v)\mu_{N,B_V}$, using [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The canonical tensor maps satisfy
$$h_{T,L_AN}\,U_T(\lambda_{u,N})\,b_{S_VN}^{-1}\,(L_Ah_{V,N})^{-1}=\mu^B_N.$$
Here is the representative check, including a possibly nonflat $B$. Choose K-flat flat-term resolutions $P\to N$ and $Q\to B_V[0]$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The pullback theorem says $L_AP,L_AQ$ are again K-flat with flat terms. The ordinary pullback/tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] on each bidegree is the canonical balanced tensor map. Under $b$ and the identifications $h$, both routes send a pullback tensor $x\otimes q$ to the pullbacks of $x$ and $q$ in the same order; after $Q\to B_V$, this is $x\otimes c$ with $c$ carried to $B_T$. This follows directly from the sectionwise tensor and its sheafification [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. These maps preserve bidegrees, so they commute with the signed total differential [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The vertical maps $P\otimes Q\to P\otimes B_V$ and $L_AP\otimes L_AQ\to L_AP\otimes B_T$ are quasi-isomorphisms since their first factors are K-flat: their cones are tensors with the acyclic resolution cones [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Cancel them after localization. Naturality under changes of resolutions and the resolving-class equivalence in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] give the displayed equality for every $N$.

proof.text:
Put $N=G_AM$, $t=S_T(\varepsilon^A_{u,M})\lambda_{u,N}:L_BS_VN\to S_TM$. By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], its B-adjunct is exactly $\chi_{u,M}$. The compatibility in [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction] says that the A-adjunct of $U_T(t)b_{S_VN}^{-1}$ is $d_{S_TM}U_V(\chi_{u,M})$. Precompose the former with $(L_Ah_{V,N})^{-1}$ and postcompose with $h_{T,M}$. Naturality of adjunction therefore makes its adjunct
$$\psi=G_A(h_{T,M})\,d_{S_TM}\,U_V(\chi_{u,M})\,h_{V,N}^{-1}.$$
By step 1 and the equality in step 3, the map being transposed is precisely
$$(\varepsilon^A_{u,M}\otimes1)\,\mu^B_{G_AM}:L_A(G_AM\otimes_A^LB_V)\longrightarrow M\otimes_A^LB_T.$$
The statement of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact], specialized to $E=M$ and $P=B_V[0]$, defines its projection transformation as the adjunct of this very map. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection gives $\psi=\pi^A_{u;M,B_V}$. No strict-perfect or boundedness hypothesis is present in that cited statement.

source.place: Tag 0B56, equation-projection-formula-map; Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), and 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition); explicit coefficient-change specialization

proof.text:
The counit formula for the mate in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] gives, before restriction of scalars,
$$\varepsilon^B_{u,S_TM}\,L_B(\chi_{u,M})=t=S_T(\varepsilon^A_{u,M})\lambda_{u,G_AM},$$
which is the asserted counit equation. All comparisons in steps 1--4 and the adjunction bijections are natural, so their displayed equality is natural in $M$. Both K-flat resolutions and the operations used above allow unbounded complexes; nowhere was $B_W$ itself assumed K-flat or $a$ flat. This proves all the claimed assertions.
